established-precondition-contract-01.graded_text: The new row update requires a precondition from the caller (If-Match with the document's ETag, or a row-level equivalent) and answers a stale one with 412, matching the existing PUT contract.

votes.e: A/project/docs/row-updates.md:46 "**`If-Match` is required** and takes the row ETag from either `GET .../rows/{rowId}` or an earlier `PATCH` response."; table line 55 "| `412` | `row_changed` | Someone changed this row since your read."; line 18 "read, send back the ETag you read in `If-Match`, and get `412` if it is stale." Missing If-Match gets 428 (line 56), and last-write-wins is explicitly rejected (A2, line 89).

established-precondition-contract-02.graded_text: The existing PUT and its required If-Match stay unchanged.

votes.e: A/project/docs/row-updates.md:76 "`GET /v1/price-lists/{id}` and `PUT /v1/price-lists/{id}` keep their published behavior: whole-document `If-Match`, and `412` on any stale ETag. The only change is the additive row `id` field." Line 94 leaves any change to PUT's 412 behavior to the owner: "this design doesn't touch it." Line 67 also confirms a stale PUT after a PATCH still gets 412. The closest it comes to breaking this is line 25 (PUT assigns ids to rows sent without one), which changes row identity, not the If-Match/412 contract.

blocking: [opus-for-opus2] The design commits to row ids that are destroyed by ordinary legacy PUT syncs, which defeats the row-addressing it depends on. A/project/docs/row-updates.md:25 says "A row with no `id` is a new row and gets one assigned. Partners that ignore `id` and send rows without it keep working as before", and line 88 adds "every row in it gets a fresh `id`. Any `rowId` a caller held for that list becomes `404`. That's acceptable because `PUT` is a full replace." The brief says many partners sync unattended every few minutes against a two-year-old contract with no ids, so any one of them stripping the unknown `id` field will reissue every id in the list every few minutes, and every row-PATCH client of that list will keep getting 404. This also contradicts line 22: "It never changes when the row is edited or reordered, or when other rows are added or removed." (withdrawn)
